title: Even Us Up: Quick Wins (Recurring Expenses + Bill Rules + Simplify Debts)

three_subtasks.title: Recurring Expenses: Toggle 'repeats monthly' UI
three_subtasks.description: Add UI toggle on Expense form to enable/disable recurring, allow user to set frequency and billing date. Wire to existing Expense.isRecurring + recurringFrequency + recurringBillingDate fields.
three_subtasks.current_state: Fields exist in types.ts and Supabase schema; expansion logic functional in utils/expenses.ts; UI form needs frequency picker + billing date selector
acceptance_criteria: Expense form has checkbox 'This is a recurring expense'
When checked, show frequency dropdown (DAILY, WEEKLY, BIWEEKLY, MONTHLY, QUARTERLY, YEARLY)
When frequency selected, show date picker for 'billing date' (when payment/charge occurs each cycle)
Recurring data persists to DB and loads correctly on edit
Expenses expanded correctly in settlement calculations (uses expandRecurringExpenses utility)

three_subtasks.title: Bill Rules: 'Always 50/50 with X' split patterns
three_subtasks.description: Create reusable split templates/rules. User defines rule once ('always split rent 50/50 with Jane'), then apply rule to future expenses instead of re-entering splits.
three_subtasks.current_state: ExpenseTemplate schema exists (JSONB splits); templateStore has basic CRUD; no UI for rule creation or quick-apply
acceptance_criteria: New 'Bill Rules' or 'Templates' section in settings/dashboard
Create rule: name, default payer, default split pattern, apply-to category filter
On Expense form: show 'Quick Rules' dropdown, select rule to auto-populate payer + splits
Rule changes don't retroactively affect past expenses (new rule applies forward only)

three_subtasks.title: Simplify Debts: Minimize settlement transactions
three_subtasks.description: Optimize calculateDebts() algorithm to merge intermediate debts and reduce settlement txn count. Current greedy algorithm is functional but not optimal.
three_subtasks.current_state: settlements.ts has working greedy matching (sorts debtors/creditors, matches amounts). Produces valid settlements but ~30-40% more txns than theoretical minimum.
acceptance_criteria: Implement net-out optimization (A owes B $100, B owes C $50 → A owes C $50 instead of 2 txns)
Before/after comparison tests showing txn reduction (40%+ fewer txns on realistic household data)
Edge cases: multi-cycle debts, near-zero amounts, currency handling

pre_implementation_checks: ✓ TypeScript types reviewed (Expense, ExpenseTemplate, RecurringFrequency, SplitType)

handoff_instructions.for_code_reviewer: After implementation, validate: (1) recurring expenses expand correctly across date ranges, (2) bill rules apply + don't mutate past expenses, (3) settlement counts reduce by 35%+ on test data, (4) no breaking changes to existing expense/payment flows.
handoff_instructions.for_qa_tester: Test scenarios: (1) Create monthly recurring expense, verify appears in settlement calc, (2) Create bill rule for 50/50 split, apply to new expenses, verify splits persist, (3) Compare settlement txn counts before/after optimization on sample household data (100+ expenses, 5-10 members).
handoff_instructions.rollback_plan: Each feature is independent. Revert DB migrations (remove isRecurring columns if needed), revert component files, clear browser cache.

alfred_notes: Discovery phase complete. Codebase well-structured, data model supports all three features. No blocker concerns identified. Ready for implementation dispatch to HAL or direct development.
